synthesis: The paper converts its RH-linked weighted-Hilbert-space closure target into an arithmetic coefficient problem in stages: the differences e_q lie in the periodic, reflection-antisymmetric subspace H_P; consecutive sine differences form an orthonormal basis of that subspace through an isometric Fourier model; and each e_q has an explicit harmonic-sum coordinate in that basis. Thus approximation of E1 becomes l2 convergence of an arithmetic coefficient array, with uniform square-summable domination as the remaining analytic burden.
source_support: Unit u01 announces the closure target, u03 constructs the orthonormal family, u04 proves it is a basis specifically of H_P by a symmetry-preserving Fourier representation, u06 proves the RH equivalence with finite e_q-combinations (using cited external inputs plus a local coefficient-sum repair), u07 computes <E_p,e_q>, and u09 states that fixed-coordinate convergence must be joined to a common square-summable majorant before dominated convergence applies.
nonparaphrase_operation: The joint mechanism restricts the functional problem to the symmetry class containing the generators, diagonalizes that class into independent basis coordinates, and translates each generator into finite arithmetic data so that functional norm convergence can be tested as l2 coefficient convergence.
limits: The Nyman-Beurling/Baez-Duarte closure equivalence and the transport isometry are cited inputs, not proved anew. The coordinate formula and several constants are extraction-sensitive, and neither the representation change nor fixed-coordinate asymptotics supplies the missing uniform l2 envelope or proves RH.
quality_reason: Accepted because the source gives an explicit dependency chain across distinct units: the closure criterion determines the target, the symmetry theorem supplies the complete coordinate system, and the generator formula plus domination discussion identifies the exact downstream proof burden. This mechanism is not available from any one parent alone and is more than a thematic combination.

synthesis: The three approximation families share the same coefficient-space strategy but localize its unresolved norm-control burden differently. The triangular family enforces exact cancellation through a growing low-coordinate block and leaves the window n < p <= n^4 after remote-tail control; the raw and exponent-smoothed Mobius families obtain the target limit only for each fixed coordinate and leave 1 <= p <= n^2 log n after their remote-tail estimates. Each resulting RH statement remains conditional on a common square-summable envelope along infinitely many n.
source_support: Units u10-u12 give the triangular coefficients, exact vanishing through p=n, the p>=n^4 majorant, and Criterion 1 on [n+1,n^4]. Units u13-u14 give fixed-p convergence to the coordinates of -E1, an O(n/p) estimate, remote domination beyond n^2 log n, and Criterion 2 on [1,n^2 log n]. Units u16-u17 establish the analogous fixed-coordinate and remote-tail conclusions for weights mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), under the stated sufficient epsilon_n conditions, and then state the matching conditional Criterion 3.
nonparaphrase_operation: Comparing the constructions separates three logically different services: exact low-mode matching, asymptotic fixed-mode targeting, and uniform control of moving coefficient mass. Boundary corrections buy exact low-block cancellation, while raw and smoothed weights retain simpler arithmetic forms but require domination starting at the first coordinate; scale estimates handle only the complementary remote tails.
limits: None of Criteria 1-3 constructs the required envelope, and coordinatewise limits plus big-O remote tails do not imply Hilbert-norm convergence. The threshold formulas and some comparison glyphs are OCR-sensitive. The Balazard statement attached to the smoothed criterion is explicitly conditional on RH and is only a calibration, not independent evidence.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parent units provide a concrete cross-scheme comparison with explicit cancellation regimes, tail thresholds, and matching sufficient criteria. The synthesis preserves the distinct sign conventions and does not upgrade finite-coordinate or remote-tail control into global l2 convergence.

synthesis: For the raw Mobius approximants, the paper turns the unresolved low-coordinate portion of the domination criterion into an exact energy calculation and derives simultaneous smallness requirements on two Mobius partial-sum combinations along any successful subsequence. The following smoothed construction changes mu(q)/q to mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), using positive epsilon_n to control truncated Dirichlet-series tails while epsilon_n tends to zero so the fixed coordinates still approach those of -E1. This is a motivated regularization of the natural scheme, not an unconditional resolution of its low-coordinate obstruction.
source_support: Units u13-u14 establish the raw family's fixed-coordinate limits, remote-tail control, and the still-required envelope through n^2 log n. Unit u15 exactly sums the energy for 2<=p<=n+1 and derives two simultaneous O(n^(-1/2)) Mobius cancellation requirements, describing them as restrictive rather than impossible. Unit u16 proves the smoothed fixed-coordinate limits and the same remote-tail regime under epsilon_n>=2 log log n/log n and epsilon_n=o(1); u17 still assumes a square-summable envelope and cites only an RH-conditional positive calibration.
nonparaphrase_operation: The energy identity compresses a growing block of coefficient errors into two arithmetic cancellation diagnostics; exponent smoothing then trades distance from the boundary exponent for absolute control of omitted Mobius tails while preserving the target fixed coordinates. Juxtaposing these mechanisms explains what smoothing changes and, equally importantly, what norm-control problem it leaves open.
limits: The exact low-energy identity applies to the unsmoothed family, and the source gives no corresponding proof that smoothing removes those unconditional cancellation demands. It does not prove the needed smoothed envelope, claim the epsilon lower bound is sharp, or rule out successful raw subsequences. Dense formulas and the extracted epsilon glyph require PDF verification before symbolic reuse, and the final efficiency result assumes RH.
quality_reason: Accepted because the obstruction and the subsequent smoothing construction form a substantive problem-response relation supported by distinct units, while the synthesis explicitly withholds the unsupported stronger claim that smoothing solves the obstruction. The preserved conditional and OCR boundaries prevent the conceptual relation from becoming a causal proof claim.

synthesis: The source uses the H_P basis theorem twice at different scales. First, periodic/reflection symmetry and an isometric Fourier rescaling identify the E_n as a complete basis of H_P. Then fractional-part folding sends an arbitrary compactly supported function into H_P, expansion in the E_n converts that folded function into the dilation-generated closure of E1, and rescaling returns an explicit approximation in the ambient space H. A cited Mellin-Wiener nonvanishing criterion gives a separate spectral explanation of the same dilation completeness.
source_support: Unit u04 characterizes H_P by two symmetries, maps it isometrically to the odd-frequency cosine sector of L2(0,1), and proves that the E_n form its orthonormal basis. Unit u05 constructs g_T by periodic fractional-part folding, invokes that basis and E_n=D_nE1-D_(n-1)E1, rescales g_T to approximate compactly supported f with a displayed error tending to zero, and separately cites the Mellin-transform criterion for density of the dilation orbit.
nonparaphrase_operation: The constructive route composes folding, symmetry-sector expansion, representation of basis elements as dilation differences, and inverse rescaling; the transform route replaces that explicit reconstruction by a nonvanishing spectral criterion. The two parents are therefore linked by direct reuse of H_P completeness rather than by a generic shared theme of bases or transforms.
limits: The explicit convergence rate belongs to the folding-and-rescaling proof, not the cited Wiener route. Density of all positive dilates of E1 in H does not establish the RH-specific closure by integer-indexed e_q generators. The extracted definition of g_T appears to interchange variables, and exact multipliers, constants, and formulas require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted because u05 materially depends on u04: the symmetry-restricted basis is the engine that converts a folded compact-support problem into a dilation approximation, while the Mellin criterion supplies an independently stated viewpoint on the resulting cyclicity. The synthesis keeps the ambient-H and restricted-H_P completeness claims separate.
